subject: Seller onboarding RFI: cloud catalog technical & procurement clauses
messages:
From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@metrocity.gov>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: AWS Partner Sales <aws-partner-sales@amazon.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: seller onboarding - AWS/Azure/GCP sections needed

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for taking the time on Friday. MetroCity is opening up our procurement packet next week and the sourcing committee has asked all shortlisted vendors to provide a focused RFI covering cloud-catalog listing and procurement requirements across AWS, Azure, and GCP.

Specifically we need:
- A short capability table that maps Redwood product features to the marketplaces' procurement clauses (billing integration, entitlements, metering, private offers).
- Evidence for security/compliance integration points (SOC2, tenant isolation, logging endpoints).
- A summary of typical commercial controls (reserved capacity, invoice flow, refunds/credits).
- Any onboarding timelines and certification steps for each marketplace.

Could you share this by COB Thursday (10/1)? Please attach any SOC / security artifacts you can share under NDA. If AWS needs to be cc'ed on any partner-specific steps, include them.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — Jordan
Procurement Lead | MetroCity Transit Authority
From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: RFI: seller onboarding - AWS/Azure/GCP sections needed

Folks — forwarding MetroCity's ask. Tight turnaround but doable. Draft plan below:

1) Create a 1-page capability mapping (AWS / Azure / GCP columns) that calls out: billing integration, entitlements, metering endpoints, private/offers, commercial flows, and expected timeline. (Owner: Lauren)
2) Pull SOC2 summary + tenancy/isolation statements and a short paragraph about log access and retention (Owner: Marcus).
3) Commercial note on reserved capacity and invoicing (examples for Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted) + suggested fallback language (Owner: Aditya).
4) Collate into a single response doc and export as both docx and PDF. I'll review and send to Jordan and cc AWS contact.

Attachments I anticipate to include: SOC2-Summary.pdf (public summary), a short Azure/GCP billing matrix (xls), and the drafted capability table. Do not include any full audit artifacts yet — we'll reference them and note NDA.

Timing: please have initial sections back to me by Wed EOD (9/30).

Thanks — Camila
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@metrocity.gov>
Cc: AWS Partner Sales <aws-partner-sales@amazon.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 11:36:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: RFI: seller onboarding - AWS/Azure/GCP sections needed

Jordan — attaching our draft response for MetroCity's procurement packet. Highlights inside:

- Capability mapping: concise table for each cloud showing what Redwood provides out-of-the-box (metering hooks, listing metadata, pricing models supported, private offers).
- Security & compliance: SOC2 summary (attachment), tenant isolation description, recommended field-level redaction patterns for PII in logs.
- Commercial flows: examples for how reserved Redwood Dedicated commitments appear on Marketplace invoices, suggested contract language for credits/refunds, and typical lead times for Dedicated provisioning (2–6 weeks depending on capacity).
- Onboarding timeline: 3-phase approach (pre-qualification, marketplace certification, go-live checklist) with expected durations per cloud.

Attachments included: RFI_Responses_CamilaDraft_v1.docx (master answers), SOC2-Summary.pdf, azure-pricing-and-billing-table.xlsx.

Notes: We flagged any customer-identifying audit artifacts as NDA-only; we can provide deeper artifacts through the legal channel if MetroCity signs the standard Redwood NDA (link in doc). If AWS has partner-specific steps (e.g. contract routing), please advise and we'll incorporate.

Would you like a short slide deck version for the sourcing committee? We can produce a 2-slide summary if helpful.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
Attachments: [RFI_Responses_CamilaDraft_v1.docx (docx), SOC2-Summary.pdf (pdf), azure-pricing-and-billing-table.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@metrocity.gov>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: AWS Partner Sales <aws-partner-sales@amazon.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RE: RFI: seller onboarding - AWS/Azure/GCP sections needed

Camila — thanks for the fast turnaround and the docx. A couple of clarifying questions from the sourcing team after an initial read:

1) For AWS private offers: can you confirm whether Redwood requires the customer to accept charges through Marketplace billing or if Redwood can invoice directly while using the AWS listing for procurement? We need explicit gating language.
2) For Azure: the spreadsheet shows billing codes but not how reserved capacity credits are handled when customer uses consumption + reserved pool. Can you provide a short example invoice line item?
3) SOC2: we appreciate the summary. For procurement we need a contactable evidence owner who can coordinate a legal review under NDA. Please provide a name and contact.

If possible, can you add short one-line answers under each question in the doc and resend? We need final RFI to attach to the procurement packet by 5pm today.

Thanks — Jordan
From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@metrocity.gov>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, AWS Partner Sales <aws-partner-sales@amazon.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: RE: RFI: seller onboarding - AWS/Azure/GCP sections needed

Jordan — appended one-line clarifications below and re-attached the updated docx (final).

1) AWS private offers: Redwood supports two commercial flows — (a) Marketplace-billed private offers where charges flow through AWS billing, and (b) Direct invoicing where the customer signs a Redwood contract and Redwood invoices directly while still maintaining a marketplace listing for procurement visibility. We note that specific procurement gating or acceptance-by-AWS may be required for (a); for (b) customers must accept Redwood-specific terms and we typically include a marketplace reference in the SOW.

2) Azure reserved credits example line: "Redwood Dedicated - Reserved Monthly Commitment: USD 12,000 | Azure Marketplace pass-through: Listing charge USD 12,000; Customer invoice shows credit line: -USD 12,000 applied from Reserved Commitment" — we'll include the spreadsheet row and a sample invoice snippet in the final PDF.

3) SOC2 evidence owner: Marcus Lin, Head of Security Integrations — marcus_lin@redwood.com. Marcus will coordinate evidence exchange under NDA and can confirm timelines (typically 3–5 business days to surface summary artifacts, longer for full audit packages).

I've attached the final RFI doc (RFI_Responses_CamilaDraft_v1.docx) and SOC2-Summary.pdf again. Please let me know if you want the two-slide executive summary, we can get that to you in under an hour.

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
Attachments: [RFI_Responses_CamilaDraft_v1.docx, SOC2-Summary.pdf]
